note: Defines how a future Claude provider would be evaluated for V0.3. No API call, account, token, or hosted model exists in this repository. Model identifiers are the candidates named for evaluation, not an integration.

candidates.why: Default candidate; evaluated first on every task.
Evaluated only as a cheaper first pass; adopted for a task class only if it meets the same quality bars as the baseline on that class.
Evaluated on the cases the baseline fails, to learn whether the difficulty is model capability or the contract; not a default.

tiers.name: select_and_order
tiers.status: the only tier proposed for V0.3

tiers.name: constrained_paraphrase
tiers.allowed_output: claim drafts that must pass the full semantic gate
tiers.status: out of scope until Tier A meets its release gate and a separate ADR accepts it

evaluation_tasks.question: Does the model choose a more useful claim order than the deterministic default, as judged by blinded human reviewers?
How often is output schema-valid, hash-consistent, decision-preserving, and complete?
Do instructions in the question or in report strings change decision, claim set, or order beyond what the contract permits?
Does the model leave ABSTAIN and ambiguity decisions to the deterministic layer?

zero_tolerance: accepted output that changes a number, identifier, unit, label, verdict or decision
accepted output that adds or removes a claim
any credential or report body written to a log
release_gate_inputs.minimum_sample: state n for every rate and report the Wilson 95% interval; a rate from fewer than 300 independent cases cannot establish a release threshold
release_gate_inputs.model_selection_rule: Choose the least expensive candidate that meets every bar above on the held-out set, then break ties on p95 latency. If no candidate beats the deterministic ordering in blinded review, ship no model.

prohibited_in_this_repository_until_v0_3: Anthropic API client or SDK dependency
API keys, tokens or environment-variable secret loading
network calls to a model provider
any claim in documentation or UI that a live model answers questions
